name: Beachhead
question: Can we win one segment repeatably, at a profitable cost?

gate.name: Repeatability
asks: Can the venture win accounts in one segment the same way, again and again?
Does each account cost less to win and serve than it brings in?
Can people other than the founder run the motion?

evidence.statement: A go-to-market record for the chosen segment
The repeatable motion written down as processes

weights.note: Unvalidated priors, ours: how much each function's open decisions count when decisions are ranked across functions in this phase. They sum to 1. The decision queue ranks with them (packages/naive/src/engine/decision-queue.ts, EE-127).

strategy.why: The segment is chosen; strategy guards the focus

products.why: The whole product for one segment

marketing-and-sales.why: Winning the segment repeatably is a go-to-market problem first

supply-chain.why: Suppliers start to matter at repeat volume

service-delivery.why: Delivering the same result to every account in the segment

customer-service.why: Keeping the accounts the segment is won with

human-capital.why: The first hires make the motion repeatable

it.why: Tools that carry the repeatable motion

finance.why: Unit economics decide whether the segment is profitable

risk-and-compliance.why: Contracts and obligations of real accounts

external-relationships.why: Investors and partners for the segment

capabilities.why: Processes written down so others can repeat them
